ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The distance between two shelves in Monika's kitchen is $36 \mathrm{~cm}$. She knows that a stack of 8 identical glasses is $42 \mathrm{~cm}$ high and a stack of 2 such glasses is $18 \mathrm{~cm}$ high. How many glasses has the biggest stack that will fit between two shelves?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows glass cups of the same shape stacked together, the cups nested into each other, so it is not that each additional cup adds one full cup height; the first cup provides the base height, and after that each additional cup only adds the same segment of exposed height. The image also shows that both the taller stack of cups and the shorter stack of cups are formed by nesting the same cups. Reasoning: Let the stacking height of n cups be H(n)=a+(n-1)d, where a is the height of the first cup, and d is the height added by each additional nested cup. It is known that H(8)=42 cm, H(2)=18 cm. Subtracting gives 42-18=24=6d, so d=4 cm. Also H(2)=a+d=18, so a=14 cm. Therefore H(n)=14+4(n-1). To fit between two layers of shelves that are 36 cm apart, it is necessary that 14+4(n-1)≤36. Solving gives 4(n-1)≤22, that is n≤6.5, so the largest integer n is 6. Check: 6 cups are 14+5×4=34 cm high, so they can fit; 7 cups are 38 cm high, so they cannot fit.

From the text, use H(8)=42 cm, H(2)=18 cm, and shelf clearance 36 cm. Set H(n)=a+(n-1)d. Subtract the two given equations: H(8)-H(2)=6d=24, so d=4 cm. method.method_draft: Use the 2-glass stack as a baseline and count extra glasses. From the image, observe that the taller stack is formed by adding more identical nested glasses to the shorter stack, with each new glass raising the stack by the same amount. From the text, the 8-glass stack is 42 cm and the 2-glass stack is 18 cm, so the 6 extra glasses add 42−18=24 cm total. Therefore each extra glass adds 24÷6=4 cm. The shelves allow 36 cm, which is 36−18=18 cm more than the 2-glass stack. Four extra glasses add 16 cm, giving 34 cm for 6 glasses; five extra glasses add 20 cm, giving 38 cm for 7 glasses, too high. Therefore the largest fitting stack has 6 glasses.
